answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a narrow work-history inlet: every new identity starts at a single inlet that only hands out tiny, publicly graded jobs, and its reputation grows like a lotus opening petal by petal, one verified job at a time. A farm must pay real compute and time for thousands of slow histories, and any bad job sends a clear signal that freezes that identity's inlet. One honest agent, by contrast, passes the same inlet once with a handful of genuine jobs, so the cost falls almost entirely on fakes, not on real newcomers.
